Post-quantum cryptography is encryption and digital signature technology designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers.
PostgreSQL product
PostgreSQL is a database system used to store and manage data.
PostHog product
PostHog is a product analytics platform used to track how people use websites and applications.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
pre-authentication concept
Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.
Pre-authentication authorization bypass technique
A flaw that lets someone bypass access checks before logging in or proving their identity.
Prescriptive controls concept
Security requirements that specify exactly which actions or technologies an organization must use.
also: fixed set of prescriptive controls, fixed, prescriptive controls
Primcloud organization
Primcloud is an organization referenced in security reporting.
Prince Group organization
Prince Group is a Cambodia-linked business group that authorities have associated with large-scale online scam operations and related criminal networks.
also: Prince Group TCO
Principles concept
High-level guiding rules or intended outcomes for making decisions and designing practices.
Prioritization concept
Prioritization means deciding which issues or tasks should be handled first based on importance or risk.
Privacy Pass protocol
Privacy Pass is a protocol that lets a service verify certain access rights without learning a user's identity.
Privacy Protection concept
Steps or tools that help keep your personal information and online activities hidden from others.
Private Access Tokens protocol
Private Access Tokens are privacy-preserving cryptographic tokens used to show a client is legitimate without revealing its identity.
Private information concept
Private information is personal or confidential data that should not be shared without permission.
private keys concept
Private keys are secret cryptographic values used to prove identity, decrypt data, or authorize cryptocurrency transactions.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
Probe technique
A probe is an attempt to test a system for weaknesses or useful information before an attack.
process[.]to other
process[.]to is a defanged internet domain referenced in security reporting, with the brackets used to prevent accidental clicking.
Production infrastructure concept
Production infrastructure is the real servers, cloud services, and systems that run live applications for users.
production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.
Profile & Action product
Profile & Action is a policy-configuration area where administrators choose how a security rule should respond.
Profiling concept
Profiling is the practice of analyzing information about someone to infer their interests, behavior, or characteristics.
Programmable logic controllers product
Programmable logic controllers are rugged industrial computers that control machines and physical processes in factories, utilities, and other environments.
also: PLCs
Project DROMOS product
A government artificial-intelligence cybersecurity initiative referenced in security reporting.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt injection technique
Prompt injection is a way of giving an AI system instructions that may make it behave in unintended ways.
also: prompt injections, indirect prompt injection
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
Proof of Human organization
An organization or project referenced in security reporting about bot detection.
also: Proof of personhood
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
Proof-of-concept exploit tool
A proof-of-concept exploit is sample code or a demonstration showing that a vulnerability can really be abused.
also: PoCs, PoC exploit
Provider action concept
A change made by an internet or service provider that affects a system's availability or connectivity.
proxies tool
Proxies are servers or devices that forward internet traffic on behalf of someone else.
also: proxy providers
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
proxy services concept
Proxy services route internet traffic through another server, often to filter, hide, monitor, or redirect connections.
Psychologically exploitative concept
Designed to take unfair advantage of people's emotions, vulnerabilities, or decision-making.
Public GitHub repository product
A public GitHub repository is a code project on GitHub that anyone on the internet can view.
Public internet concept
The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
Public Link concept
A public link is a web link that allows anyone with the link, and sometimes anyone online, to access a shared item.
public projects concept
Public projects are code repositories or workspaces that anyone can view, and sometimes copy or interact with.
Public repositories concept
Public repositories are online code storage spaces that anyone can view.
public repository concept
A public repository is an online code or file storage area that anyone can view and sometimes copy from.
public sector organization
Government organizations and publicly funded services.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.
public-facing applications concept
Public-facing applications are websites, portals, or services that people on the internet can reach, making them common targets for attackers.
Publicly disclosed concept
Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.
pull technique
To download a container image from a container repository.
pull request concept
A pull request is a request to review and merge code changes into a shared software project.
also: pull requests
pull-request-target technique
pull-request-target is a GitHub Actions trigger that runs in the context of the target repository and can expose sensitive permissions if used carelessly.
pwn-request technique
A pwn-request is an attack or risky pattern where pull request automation is abused to compromise a software project.
Pwn2Own Vancouver organization
A hacking competition in Vancouver where researchers demonstrate and report vulnerabilities in widely used products.
Python runtime concept
A Python runtime is the software environment needed to execute Python programs.
Python SimpleHTTP tool
Python SimpleHTTP refers to Python’s simple built-in web server often used to quickly serve files over HTTP.
Python-based information stealer malware
A Python-based information stealer is malware written in Python that steals sensitive data such as passwords, files, or browser information.
PZZ tool
PZZ is a custom AI-driven hacking framework referenced in security reporting.
QiAnXin Technology Group organization
QiAnXin Technology Group is a Chinese cybersecurity company that operates the XLab research team.
Quarantining a File technique
Quarantining a file means isolating it so users cannot access or share it until it is reviewed or released.
Queens Public Library organization
A public library system serving the Queens borough of New York City.
also: QPL, The library system, the library
Queue concept
A queue is a line of tasks or messages waiting to be processed in order.
queues concept
Queues are ordered waiting lines for tasks or messages that computer systems process one at a time or in sequence.
Radiflow organization
Radiflow is a cybersecurity company focused on protecting industrial and operational technology networks.
Radiflow CIARA product
Radiflow CIARA is an industrial cybersecurity product used to model assets, attack paths, and risk-reduction options.
Railway product
Railway is a cloud hosting platform used to deploy applications and services.
Rakefile tool
A configuration file containing automated build or task instructions for Ruby's Rake tool.
ransom concept
A sum of money demanded by criminals to restore access to data or systems after a ransomware attack.
ransom demands concept
Ransom demands are requests from criminals for payment, usually in exchange for restoring access to stolen or encrypted data.
ransom notes concept
Ransom notes are messages from attackers demanding payment, usually after data has been encrypted or stolen.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
also: Ransomware gangs, ransomware attacks
ransomware attack concept
A ransomware attack is when criminals lock files or systems and demand payment to restore access or prevent data leaks.
Ransomware gang threat-actor
A ransomware gang is a criminal group that uses malware or data theft to demand payment from victims.
ransomware group threat-actor
A ransomware group is a criminal or threat-actor team that uses malware to lock or steal data and demand payment.
Rate limits technique
Rate limits are rules that restrict how many requests a person or program can make in a set time.
rate-limiting concept
Rate-limiting restricts how many requests someone can make in a set time to prevent abuse or overload.
RCE vulnerability
RCE, or remote code execution, is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands or programs on someone else's system from afar.
reachability concept
Reachability means whether one system, account, or network location can access another.
Read-Only concept
A permission setting that allows someone to view information but not change it.
Read-Only Access concept
Read-only access lets someone view information but not change, create, or delete it.
Read-Only Mode concept
A setting that allows files or storage to be viewed and copied but prevents changes from being saved.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
Recover concept
Recover means restoring systems and business operations after a cyber incident.
Red Heron threat-actor
A suspected China-linked threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
Redamon other
A named entity referenced in security reporting about ARTEX.
redirect concept
A redirect sends a browser or request from one web address to another.
redirects concept
Redirects are instructions that automatically send a user or browser from one web address to another.
reflection technique
Reflection is a technique where an attacker bounces traffic or responses off another system, often to hide the source or amplify an attack.
Refrigeration Controllers product
Devices that monitor and control cooling equipment, including temperatures and defrost settings.
also: refrigeration units
Refrigeration Controls product
Computerized systems that monitor and control refrigeration equipment such as fridges and freezers.
Refrigeration Systems product
Refrigeration systems are equipment that keep food or other goods cold at controlled temperatures.
Refrigerators product
Machines that keep food or other goods cold to slow spoilage.
also: freezers
remediate concept
To remediate means to fix a security problem or reduce the risk it creates.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
also: remediation process
Remediation workflows concept
Remediation workflows are planned steps for fixing security issues after they are found.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
also: necessary remote access
remote access tool tool
A remote access tool is software that lets someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote access tooling tool
Software that lets someone connect to and control a computer from another location.
remote code execution flaw vulnerability
A remote code execution flaw is a serious bug that can let an attacker run commands on a system from somewhere else over a network.
remote command execution vulnerability
Remote command execution is when an attacker can run operating-system commands on another computer over a network.
Remote monitoring concept
Using network-connected systems to observe equipment or conditions from another location.
also: automated and remote monitoring of temperatures
Remote root RCE technique
A vulnerability or attack that lets someone remotely run commands with the system's highest administrator privileges.
also: remote root code execution
remote servers concept
Remote servers are computers located elsewhere on a network or the internet that provide data, services, or control to other devices.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
also: authenticated command execution, pre-authentication remote code execution
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
Render product
Render is a cloud platform for hosting websites, applications, and backend services.
Replayed technique
Replayed means captured data, such as a token or request, is sent again to try to repeat an action or gain access.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
also: repositories
repository history concept
Repository history is the record of changes made to a software project's files over time.
Repository secrets concept
Repository secrets are sensitive values such as passwords, tokens, or API keys stored for use with a code repository or its automation tools.
Reputation concept
A trust score or history used by security systems to judge whether a sender, website, or file is likely safe.
also: User reputation
request parameter concept
A request parameter is a piece of information sent to a website or application as part of a request.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
Response concept
Response is the part of cybersecurity where an organization investigates, contains, and recovers from a security incident.
Responsible disclosure concept
Responsible disclosure is the practice of privately reporting a security flaw to the vendor so it can be fixed before details are widely shared.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
restore_all other
A software function name that indicates it restores all data or components from a backup.
Restrictive Action concept
A restrictive action is a security response that limits access to data or a service when a rule is broken.
also: immediate restrictive action, follow-up action, immediate action
Retries concept
Repeated attempts by software to complete an operation after an earlier attempt failed.
reverse proxy tool
A reverse proxy is a server that sits in front of other servers and forwards user requests to them, often adding security or load balancing.
Revoke technique
To cancel a credential, permission, or access key so it can no longer be used.
Revoking Access technique
Revoking access means removing someone's permission to view, edit, or use a resource.
also: revoking access from specific users, lose access
risk analysis concept
Risk analysis is the process of estimating how likely a problem is and how much harm it could cause.
robots.txt protocol
robots.txt is a website file that gives web crawlers instructions about which pages they should or should not crawl.
romance concept
Romance refers to romantic relationships or dating contexts, which criminals may exploit in romance scams to manipulate victims.
romance scam technique
A romance scam is a fraud where criminals pretend to build a romantic relationship to steal money or information.
Romance schemes concept
Fraud scams in which criminals build a fake romantic relationship to steal money or information.
root concept
The superuser account on Unix and Linux systems that has unlimited control over the entire computer.
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
also: gain root access
Root code execution technique
Root code execution means an attacker can run commands with the highest level of control on a Unix-like system.
root privileges concept
Root privileges are the highest level of control on Unix-like systems, allowing a user or program to change almost anything.
root shell concept
A root shell is a command-line session with the highest administrator privileges on a Unix or Linux system.
Root-command execution technique
The ability to run commands with the highest level of control on a Unix-like system.
Root-in-Cloud vulnerability
Google's top vulnerability category for flaws that could give an attacker full control of cloud organizations or projects.
also: root-in-prod
RSA Signature concept
An RSA signature is a cryptographic check that helps prove data came from a holder of a private key and was not altered.
Ruby tool
Ruby is a programming language used to build software and web applications.
rubygems
RubyGems is the package manager and public package repository for the Ruby programming language.
also: Ruby Gems
RubyGems and Bundler 4.0.23 product
A specific release version of the RubyGems package manager and Bundler dependency-management tool.
also: 4.0.x, stable 4.0.x
RubyGems and Bundler 4.1.0.beta3 product
A prerelease version of the RubyGems package manager and Bundler dependency-management tool.
also: 4.1.0.beta3
RubyGems packages product
RubyGems packages are reusable software bundles for the Ruby programming language that developers can install from package repositories.
RubyGems plugins tool
Special Ruby gems that can add behavior to RubyGems commands and may load code automatically.
RubyGems security team organization
The group responsible for receiving and addressing security reports affecting the RubyGems ecosystem.
rubygems_plugin.rb tool
A specially named Ruby file that can cause a gem to be loaded as a RubyGems plugin.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
runner tool
A machine or service that executes automated jobs in a CI/CD pipeline, which if compromised can be used to inject malicious code into builds.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
Runtime Telemetry concept
Data collected about what software does while it is running, such as actions, errors, and resource use.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
also: Moscow, Kremlin
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service organization
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service is Russia's civilian foreign intelligence agency, also known as the SVR.
Russia-linked threat-actor
A description for threat actors or activity reported as having connections to Russia.
Russian government organization
The Russian government is Russia's national governing organization and is often mentioned in cyber and geopolitical reporting.
Safari product
Apple's web browser that comes pre-installed on Macs, iPhones, and iPads.
Safari 17.5 product
A version of Safari, Apple's web browser for its devices.
safe mode concept
Safe mode is a limited startup mode that runs a device with only essential software to help diagnose problems.
Safe Remediation technique
A controlled process for testing, approving, applying, and checking security changes to systems.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
SAM RPC protocol
SAM RPC is a Windows remote-procedure interface used to manage local accounts and security-account information.
sampling technique
Sampling means examining a portion of data or events instead of reviewing every single item.
sanctioned concept
Sanctioned means officially restricted or penalized by a government, often by banning business dealings or freezing assets.
sanctions concept
Government-imposed restrictions that block or limit trade, financial dealings, or travel with targeted individuals or countries.
also: designations
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
also: sandboxed frames, HTML sandbox, HTML-preview sandbox, sandboxed page
sandbox restrictions technique
Sandbox restrictions are limits that keep software or code confined so it cannot freely affect the rest of a computer or network.

A technique where malware breaks out of a restricted, isolated testing environment to attack the real underlying system.
sandboxed concept
Sandboxed means running software in a restricted environment so it has limited access to the rest of the system.
sandboxed environment concept
A sandboxed environment is a restricted place where software can run with limits to reduce the damage it can cause.
Saved Wi-Fi Passwords concept
Saved Wi-Fi passwords are network passwords stored on a device so it can reconnect automatically.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
scam centers organization
Scam centers are organized workplaces where criminals run fraud schemes, often using phones, messaging apps, or fake websites.
scam compounds concept
Scam compounds are physical locations where organized groups run large-scale online fraud operations, often using coerced labor.
also: cyber scam compound workers, jail-like facilities
Scam messages concept
Scam messages are texts, emails, or chats designed to trick people into sending money, data, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
Scattered Spider threat-actor
Scattered Spider is a cybercrime group known for social engineering, account theft, and high-profile intrusions.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
ScopeSentry tool
An asset-discovery and vulnerability-scanning platform used to identify systems and potential security weaknesses.
ScopeWeaver tool
A security tool described as a rebranded version of the ARTEX reconnaissance platform.
screenshot concept
A screenshot is a captured image of what is shown on a screen.
Seattle Public Library organization
The public library system serving Seattle, Washington.
secret scanners tool
Secret scanners are tools that look through code or files for exposed passwords, API keys, and other sensitive credentials.
secret scanning technique
Secret scanning is the automated search for exposed passwords, API keys, tokens, and other sensitive credentials in code or files.
secrets concept
Secrets are private values such as passwords, tokens, or keys used to access systems or services.
also: protected credentials
Section 230 other
A U.S. legal provision that generally protects online platforms from liability for content posted by users.
Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act concept
A U.S. law provision that generally limits online platforms' liability for content posted by users.
security coverage concept
Security coverage is the extent to which an organization's systems are protected by security controls and policies.
Security essentials concept
Basic knowledge and practices needed to protect accounts, devices, systems, and information.
Security flaws concept
Weaknesses or mistakes in software or systems that attackers may be able to exploit.
security gaps concept
Weaknesses or missing protections in a system's defense that can be exploited by attackers to gain unauthorized access.
Security impact concept
Security impact is the real harm or access that a security weakness or attack can cause.
Security incidents concept
Security incidents are events that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems or data.
security issue concept
A problem that could let someone access, alter, disrupt, or expose a system or its data improperly.
Security outcomes concept
The desired security results an organization aims to achieve, rather than a fixed list of technical steps.
also: enduring security outcomes, cybersecurity outcomes
security patch concept
A security patch is a software update that fixes a vulnerability or weakness attackers could exploit.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
Security Questions concept
Security questions are backup login checks that ask for personal answers, such as a first pet or birthplace.
Security relevant concept
Security relevant means important to protecting systems or understanding risk.
Security Skills concept
Knowledge and abilities used to protect systems, investigate threats, and respond to incidents.
security software product
Security software is software designed to protect computers, networks, or data from threats.
Security Spending concept
Security Spending is the money an organization uses for cybersecurity staff, tools, services, and programs.
Security team organization
A security team is the group of people responsible for protecting an organization's systems and data.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security testing concept
Security testing is checking software, systems, or networks to find weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
Seed Phrase concept
A seed phrase is a list of secret words that can restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet.
segmentation technique
Segmentation is dividing a network or system into separate parts to limit how far an attacker can move.
Sekoia organization
Sekoia is a cybersecurity company known for threat intelligence and security operations products.
Self Service+ product
Self Service+ is a product that lets employees handle some common technology tasks without waiting for IT support.
self-hosted concept
Self-hosted means an organization runs software on servers it controls instead of using a vendor's cloud service.

Self-registration is a feature that lets people create their own accounts without an administrator manually creating them.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive files concept
Sensitive files are files that contain private, secret, or valuable information that should not be exposed to unauthorized people.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.

A server migration is the process of moving a server, application, or its data to a different system or environment.

A web vulnerability where attacker-controlled text is processed as server template code, possibly allowing command execution or data theft.

A service desk is a support team that handles user requests, technical issues, and account help.
Service desk agents concept
Service desk agents are support staff who help users with account, device, or technical problems and may be targeted by attackers.
service providers organization
Service providers are companies or organizations that deliver services such as internet access, hosting, software platforms, or managed IT support.
Session access concept
Session access means the ability to use an active logged-in session, sometimes allowing someone to act as that user without knowing the password.
session information concept
Data that keeps a user logged in and records details about their current interaction with a service.
Set Time Trigger product
A policy setting that delays a follow-up security action until a chosen amount of time has passed.
also: time trigger
Setup concept
The process of preparing a device, application, or account for use.
severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.
Severity Score concept
A severity score is a rating that helps show how serious a security flaw or incident is.
severity scores concept
Severity scores rate how serious a vulnerability or security finding is.
shadow-ai

shared chat concept
A shared chat is a conversation that has been made available for other people to view through a link or collaboration feature.
also: shared ChatGPT conversation, shared ChatGPT link, public ChatGPT share link, shared chats

A shared credential is a password, token, or other login secret used by more than one person or system.
shared credentials concept
Shared credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used by more than one person or system.
sharepoint

SharePoint Server product
SharePoint Server is Microsoft’s on-premises collaboration and document-management platform for organizations.
SharePoint ToolShell vulnerability
SharePoint ToolShell is a name used for vulnerabilities and exploitation activity affecting Microsoft SharePoint servers.
Sharing links concept
Sharing links are web links that give other people access to a file, folder, or online resource.
shell tool

Shell command injection is a vulnerability where attackers make an application run operating-system commands it should not run.
shell commands concept
Shell commands are text instructions typed into a command line to tell a computer what to do.

Shell companies are legal business entities that often have little real activity and can be used to hide who controls money or operations.
also: shell-company networks
shell company organization
A company with little or no real business activity that may be used to hold assets or hide transactions.

Shell history is the saved list of commands a user typed in a command-line terminal.

A security tool that gathers and analyzes logs from across an organization in real time to spot suspicious activity.
SIGBUS concept
SIGBUS is an operating-system signal that usually means a program tried to access invalid memory.
Sign-In concept
Sign-in is the process of proving your identity to access a computer, account, or online service.
signing technique
A cryptographic process that uses a private key to prove that data came from its owner and was not changed.
skill concept
A voice-driven application that adds capabilities to a smart assistant like Amazon Alexa, similar to an app on a phone.
SkyW4lker tool

SleeperGem malware
SleeperGem is a named malware or software supply-chain threat referenced in security reporting.
also: SleeperGem campaign
smart TVs product

SMS is the standard text messaging service used on mobile phones.

SOC analysis concept
SOC analysis is the work security operations center analysts do to investigate alerts and detect threats.
social engineering technique

social media concept
Social media means online platforms where people share messages, photos, videos, and other content.
Social media platforms product
Social media platforms are online services where people create profiles, share content, and communicate with others.

Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.

A newer version of software that may add improvements or fix problems and security flaws.
software updates concept
Software updates are new versions or fixes released to improve features, repair bugs, or close security holes.
Software Versions concept
Numbered releases of a software product that identify which update or build is installed.
Sophisticated Exploits concept
Advanced methods or code that attackers use to take advantage of a software weakness.
source code repository tool
A source code repository is a storage location where software code and its change history are kept.
south-korea
South Korea is an East Asian country often referenced in cybersecurity stories involving technology, espionage, or regional threats.
Spam_Config other
A named software backup component associated with spam-configuration data.
spearphishing technique
Spearphishing is a targeted scam message sent to a specific person or group to trick them into giving access or information.
spearphishing-link
A spearphishing link is a targeted phishing message that includes a malicious link tailored to a specific person or organization.
also: Phishing: Spearphishing Link

Highly trained military units that carry out specialized missions such as reconnaissance, counterterrorism, and training partner forces.
Specops Password Policy product
Specops Password Policy is a product that helps organizations enforce stronger password rules in Microsoft Active Directory.
Specops Secure Service Desk product
Specops Secure Service Desk is a product that helps verify users securely during help desk password resets and support requests.
Specops Software organization
A company that provides password management and authentication solutions for enterprises.

spoofed technique
Spoofed means faked to look like it came from a trusted person, system, or address.
spray objects technique
An exploitation technique that places many similar objects in memory to make a bug easier to exploit reliably.
spyware malware
Spyware is malicious or intrusive software that secretly monitors a person’s device, messages, location, or activity.

sshd tool
sshd is the server program that provides remote access to a computer using SSH.
also: server
stable concept

state-linked concept
State-linked describes activity believed to be connected to or supported by a national government.
steal information technique

stepsecurity organization

Stockfish tool
A powerful open-source chess engine that analyzes chess positions and suggests moves.
Stolen concept
Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen accounts concept
